question.problem: The function $f(x)={e}^{x+k}+3$ has an inverse function given by ${f}^{-1}(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)+5.$ What is the value of $k?$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={e}^{x+k}+3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={e}^{y+k}+3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={e}^{y+k}+3 \\ {e}^{y+k} & =x-3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{y+k}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3) \\ y+k & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3) \\ y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)-k\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)-k.$

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=-5.$
